edges.description: Growth can encroach on the residual lumen.

Inflammatory proteases can degrade the matrix of an established plaque.
Advanced plaque can develop an immature microvascular network.
Lumen encroachment produces the defining imaging phenotype.
Severe stenosis can impair distal perfusion when compensatory flow is inadequate.
Loss of cap matrix increases vulnerability to rupture.
Fragile microvessels permit red-cell leakage into the plaque.
Hemorrhagic plaque remodeling increases vulnerability.
A weakened cap is more susceptible to rupture or ulceration.
Surface injury provides the substrate for platelet adhesion and coagulation.
Surface thrombus can fragment and travel distally.
Emboli obstruct downstream vessels and compromise tissue perfusion.
Sustained cerebral ischemia can progress to infarction.
Transient cerebral ischemia produces focal neurologic symptoms.
Transient retinal ischemia produces transient monocular visual loss.
Hemodynamic impairment is measured as delayed contrast arrival.
Smoking and diet are named as the lifestyle factors playing the largest role in carotid plaque development, which is the node this exposure acts on.

evidence.snippet: The characteristic lesion of atherosclerosis is the atherosclerotic plaque or atheromatous plaque, a complex lesion of the intimal layer of the vessel wall, consisting of a central core of cholesterol clefts, macrophages, and inflammatory cells, surrounded by layers of smooth muscle cells and connective tissue as well as a fibrous cap separating the core from the arterial lumen.

nodes.description: Endothelial dysfunction in the carotid arterial wall permits infiltration and retention of apoB-containing lipoproteins in the intima. Retained LDL is modified locally and initiates the inflammatory plaque-forming branch of atherosclerotic carotid stenosis.

evidence.reference_title: The Role of Lipids and Lipoproteins in Atherosclerosis.
evidence.snippet: infiltration and retention of apoB containing lipoproteins in the artery wall is a critical initiating event that sparks an inflammatory response and promotes the development of atherosclerosis.

nodes.description: Recruited carotid-intimal monocytes become macrophages, internalize modified apoB lipoproteins, and form lipid-laden foam cells. Macrophage inflammation amplifies LDL oxidation, endothelial activation, and additional monocyte recruitment in the plaque-forming branch.

evidence.snippet: Carotid stenosis (CS) is a buildup of atherosclerotic plaque within the artery leading to a wide range of symptoms, from mild symptoms, including blurred vision and confusion, to much more life-threatening presentations, including paralysis due to stroke.

nodes.description: Carotid stenting with embolic protection is an alternative for selected patients. CREST found similar composite outcomes to endarterectomy but more periprocedural stroke with stenting and more myocardial infarction with endarterectomy, with age modifying relative outcomes. In the separate CREST-2 stenting trial for asymptomatic stenosis of at least 70%, transfemoral stenting plus intensive management reduced the 4-year composite from 6.0% to 2.8% (P=.02). Certified operators and trial selection limit generalization; CREST-2 did not include TCAR or directly compare stenting with endarterectomy.

evidence.reference_title: Stenting versus endarterectomy for treatment of carotid-artery stenosis.
evidence.snippet: the rates of the individual end points differed between the stenting group and the endarterectomy group (death, 0.7% vs. 0.3%; P = 0.18; stroke, 4.1% vs. 2.3%; P = 0.01; myocardial infarction, 1.1% vs. 2.3%; P = 0.03)

evidence.reference_title: Medical Management and Revascularization for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis.
evidence.snippet: In the stenting trial, the 4-year incidence of primary-outcome events was 6.0% (95% confidence interval [CI], 3.8 to 8.3) in the medical-therapy group and 2.8% (95% CI, 1.5 to 4.3) in the stenting group

nodes.description: Carotid endarterectomy removes the atheromatous lesion. NASCET established benefit for selected recently symptomatic 70-99% stenosis; prompt assessment is important, with timing depending on neurologic stability and infarct burden. Older ACAS results supported selected asymptomatic patients, but in the separate modern CREST-2 endarterectomy trial the 4-year composite rate was 3.7% with surgery plus intensive management versus 5.3% with intensive management alone (P=.24). This neutral asymptomatic result does not negate symptomatic-trial benefit.

evidence.snippet: Patients with asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis of 60% or greater reduction in diameter and whose general health makes them good candidates for elective surgery will have a reduced 5-year risk of ipsilateral stroke if carotid endarterectomy performed with less than 3% perioperative morbidity and mortality is added to aggressive management of modifiable risk factors.
